text:
amy: Heads-up — large customer (healthcare) just asked for cryptographic proof that audit events are generated, immutable, and delivered. They want per-tenant signed event bundles + retention guarantees before signing the BAA. Any quick thoughts on gaps?
rajesh: Important questions: 1) do they want signing at ingest or signing-on-export? 2) do we need KMS-backed signing (customer CMK) or is HMAC with our KMS ok?
sarah: Legal: for BAA/FedRAMP-style asks they usually require customer control or at least attested key custody. Customer CMK or HSM-backed proofs are preferable. Also need SLAs for delivery/availability of evidence.
lisa: Customer specifically asked: "we need verifiable chain of events for admin changes (RBAC), model version rollouts, and key-ops related to KMS wraps." They called out RBAC change events not showing enough context in current schema.
amy: Summary of gaps I've seen: - event payloads miss actor_id context for role changes - no event version field for schema migration - export bundles are not signed today - sampling/backfill not easy to produce on demand
rajesh: Tech options we discussed before: - Attach `signature` field signed by our KMS key on each event at emit time. Pros: simple verification, per-event proof. Cons: huge storage + per-token signing perf.
rajesh: - Batch-signed daily bundles per-tenant with a digest merkle root. Pros: compact, can sign once. Cons: latency before proof available, harder for immediate incident triage.
amy: Customer asked for both: immediate proofs for admin actions, and daily bundles for bulk telemetry. So hybrid approach seems likely.
amy: Proposed quick schema snippet for admin change event (we should version):
```json
{
  "event_id": "uuid",
  "event_type": "rbac.change",
  "event_version": "v2",
  "actor_id": "u-12345",
  "actor_role_at_time": "org-admin",
  "target_user": "u-54321",
  "changes": {"from":"viewer","to":"editor"},
  "kms_key_id": "projects/.../locations/.../keyRings/.../cryptoKeys/...",
  "signature": "base64(sig)",
  "issued_at": "2025-06-12T15:01:02Z"
}
```
rajesh: Note `kms_key_id` could be optional if customer uses our signing key. We should add `event_version` and `schema_uri` for forward compatibility.
sarah: Also surface what we can guarantee contractually: - retention window (days) - proof generation latency - key custodianship model (redacted if customer CMK) - acceptance tests (sample events) that customer can run to validate delivery/format
lisa: On acceptance tests: customer wants a reproducible flow where they trigger an RBAC change and get a signed event within X minutes, plus an API to fetch signed bundles for a date range.
amy: For RBAC changes we must ensure service side generates enriched context: admin session id, impersonation flag, source IP, deploy id if change done by automation. Otherwise auditors will flag gaps.
rajesh: Implementation concerns: per-event signing at emit path requires KMS latency budget. We can use an async signing queue: write event, return 200, then sign and attach signature; but customers asked for immediate proof for admin ops — async may fail acceptance tests.
amy: Could use ephemeral HMAC with per-tenant secret cached on servers (rotation via KMS) to avoid per-event KMS calls. That gives low latency but customer CMK scenario fails.
sarah: If customer insists on holding CMK, we need to document: 1) key usage policy, 2) rotation/escrow rules, 3) what happens if key revoked (we need re-sign/backfill story).
audit-bot: Deploy note: signature-service v0.3 rolled to staging today — supports batch signing and single-event HMACs. Logs: `sigsvc: queued 128 events for tenant t-987` (reacts :eyes:)
lisa: Can we offer a contractual SLA: "signed event appearance within 5 minutes for admin events"? Ops feasibility?
rajesh: 5 minutes might be okay for signed-bundle availability if we rely on fast queue + parallel workers. For per-event KMS-based signing, 5s per event is possible with warm connections but scale/cost is large. Need SRE run numbers.
amy: Also discuss retention and export: customers want signed bundles available for 7 years in some cases. We need legal + storage plan for long-term signed artifacts (immutable storage & proof-of-non-repudiation).
sarah: Long retention increases liabilities. We should propose tiers: default 90 days, extended (paid) 7 years with custody agreement. Also require watermarking of exported bundles (hashes stored on WORM storage).
rajesh: Edge cases: 1) RBAC rollback events — we must track prior state snapshots to prove what changed. 2) Tenant deletion requests — do we delete event proofs? If a customer deletes data under GDPR, we need policy for signed bundles (can't delete cryptographic receipts without losing proof).
amy: For FedRAMP-like requests they'll want signed audit bundles plus chain-of-custody logs for KMS operations (key creation, rotation, wrap/unwrap events). We need to ensure KMS operations are included in our audit stream.
\lsarah: (typo) — Sarah: Also tie incident response. If customer claims evidence missing, we need a reproducible triage run: show ingestion logs, worker processing traces, signature issuance timeline, and export hash. That should map to contractual liability clauses.
lisa: Action items: 1) define event schema v2 for admin/model/kms ops (amy) 2) prototype hybrid signing: HMAC per-event + daily signed merkle bundles (rajesh) 3) Legal to draft BAA appendix w/ key custody options + SLA (sarah) 4) Customer acceptance test plan + sample harness (lisa)
amy: I'll draft schema today — will include `event_version`, `schema_uri`, `actor_context`, `signature_metadata` (signer_key, method, algorithm), and `delivery_proof` (bundle_id, merkle_root) fields.
rajesh: I'll spin up a staging job to generate a synthetic tenant run and measure latency/cost for per-event signing vs HMAC. Will post numbers.
sarah: I'll draft the contract appendix and propose two pathways: A) customer-managed CMK with higher price + limits; B) provider-managed signing with attestations.
audit-bot: CI note: created issue SIG-412: "signed-audit-proofs: schema + acceptance-tests" — link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sig/issues/412
amy: Thanks — once I have the schema draft I'll ping @sarah and @rajesh and attach example signed bundle flow for the acceptance test.
rajesh: One more operational ask: add an `evidence_request_id` in events so export API can return deterministic bundles for specific legal requests. Makes triage easier.
amy: Good call. I'll include `evidence_request_id` as optional.
lisa: Customer meeting scheduled Thursday 10am PT — we should have the schema draft + high-level SLA options by then.
sarah: Agreed. I'll prepare the contract appendix draft by EOD Wednesday.
rajesh: I'll have initial perf numbers by Tuesday afternoon.
amy: Cool — locking this thread. If anyone hits blockers DM me. :thumbsup:
